title: Canadian Pancakes
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Tender, golden pancakes served with butter and pure Canadian maple syrup.
ingredients: butter and pure maple syrup, to serve
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl until the leavening is evenly distributed.
Whisk the eggs, milk and melted butter in a second bowl, then pour the mixture into the dry ingredients.
Stir only until no dry flour remains; small lumps keep the pancakes tender rather than tough.
Heat a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat and spoon in portions of batter with room to spread.
Cook until bubbles appear and the underside is golden, then flip once and finish the second side.
Keep finished pancakes warm briefly, stack them, and serve with butter and pure maple syrup.
tips: Do not press pancakes with a spatula after turning.
substitutions: Use a neutral plant milk if needed.
storage: Refrigerate cooled pancakes for up to three days and reheat gently.

title: Blueberry Pancakes
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Fluffy breakfast pancakes folded with blueberries and finished with maple syrup.
ingredients: butter and maple syrup, to serve
instructions: Combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl, breaking up any lumps in the baking powder.
Whisk eggs, milk and melted butter together until smooth, then add them to the dry mixture.
Fold the batter just until combined and gently fold in the blueberries without crushing them.
Cook rounds of batter on a medium-hot buttered griddle until bubbles set around the edges.
Turn once, cook until golden and cooked through, and keep the finished pancakes warm.
Serve the pancakes with butter, extra blueberries and maple syrup while hot.
tips: Add frozen berries straight from the freezer.
commonMistakes: Stirring until the batter is completely smooth.
substitutions: Use raspberries in place of blueberries.
storage: Freeze separated pancakes for up to two months.

title: Maple French Toast
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Golden brioche French toast with warm maple syrup and butter.
ingredients: pure maple syrup and berries, to serve
instructions: Whisk eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a shallow dish until no streaks of egg remain.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and melt enough butter to coat its surface.
Dip each brioche slice briefly on both sides so it absorbs custard without becoming fragile.
Place the soaked slices in the hot skillet without crowding and cook until deeply golden underneath.
Turn carefully and cook the other side until the centre is set and the bread is warmed through.
Serve immediately with butter, berries and warmed pure maple syrup.
tips: Use day-old brioche for the best texture.
commonMistakes: Soaking fresh soft bread for too long.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers and reheat in a skillet.

title: Saskatoon Berry Pie
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A classic Canadian prairie pie filled with juicy Saskatoon berries and lemon.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a 9-inch pie plate with one round of chilled pastry.
Mix the berries with sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, cinnamon and salt until every berry is coated.
Spoon the filling into the pastry shell and dot the surface with butter for a glossy filling.
Add the top crust or lattice, seal the edges well, cut vents, and brush lightly with beaten egg.
Bake until the crust is richly golden and the berry filling bubbles thickly through the vents.
Cool completely before slicing so the natural berry juices and starch set into clean slices.
tips: Bake the pie on a tray to catch any bubbling juices.
commonMistakes: Cutting the pie while the filling is still hot.
substitutions: Use a prepared double pie crust if desired.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to three days.

title: Date Squares
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Buttery oat crumble bars with a soft, bright date filling.
instructions: Simmer the dates, water and lemon juice until the dates are soft, then stir in vanilla and cool the filling.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line a square baking pan with parchment, leaving an overhang for lifting.
Rub oats, flour, brown sugar, butter, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together until a coarse crumble forms.
Press about two-thirds of the crumb mixture firmly into the lined pan to make an even base.
Spread the cooled date filling over the base, then scatter the remaining crumble evenly over the top.
Bake until golden, cool fully, chill briefly for sharp edges, and cut into squares.
tips: Let the filling cool before layering it over the crumb base.
commonMistakes: Cutting before the bars have fully set.
substitutions: Use orange juice in place of lemon juice.
storage: Refrigerate airtight for up to five days.

title: Gingerbread Cookies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Spiced, crisp-edged gingerbread cookies for decorating and sharing.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking soda, ginger, cinnamon, cloves and salt together so the spices are evenly dispersed.
Cream butter and brown sugar until light, then beat in the egg and molasses until smooth.
Mix in the dry ingredients only until a dough forms, then divide, wrap, and chill until firm.
Roll chilled dough on a lightly floured surface, cut shapes, and transfer them to lined baking sheets.
Bake at 350°F until the edges are set but the centres are not overbaked, then cool on racks.
Decorate completely cooled cookies with icing only after their surfaces are dry and firm.
tips: Chill the dough again if it softens while rolling.
commonMistakes: Adding too much flour while rolling.
substitutions: Decorate with a simple lemon glaze.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for one week.

title: Maple Cookies
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: Soft maple sandwich cookies with a creamy maple filling.
instructions: Whisk flour, baking powder and salt together and set the mixture aside while preparing the cookie base.
Cream butter and brown sugar, then beat in the egg, maple syrup and vanilla until silky.
Mix in the flour mixture just until a soft dough forms and chill it briefly for easier shaping.
Scoop or roll even portions onto lined trays and bake at 350°F until the edges are lightly coloured.
Beat the filling butter, icing sugar and maple syrup until smooth, then let the cookies cool completely.
Spread or pipe filling onto half the cookies and sandwich with the remaining cookies before serving.
tips: Match cookie halves by size before filling.
commonMistakes: Filling cookies before they are cool.
substitutions: Make drop cookies instead of using a maple-leaf cutter.
storage: Keep airtight at cool room temperature for three days.

title: Blueberry Grunt
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A Nova Scotian stovetop dessert of bubbling blueberries and tender steamed biscuits.
instructions: Stir blueberries, sugar, lemon juice, zest and cornstarch together in a wide saucepan over medium heat.
Cook until the berries release juice and the sauce begins to bubble and thicken around the fruit.
Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, then rub in cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Stir in milk just until a sticky biscuit dough comes together without overworking it.
Drop small spoonfuls over the simmering blueberries, cover tightly, and steam until the biscuits are cooked through.
Serve the warm blueberry grunt promptly with cream or vanilla ice cream if desired.
tips: Keep the lid closed while the biscuits steam.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lid repeatedly during steaming.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers for two days and reheat gently.

title: Strawberry Rhubarb Crisp
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
description: A ruby strawberry-rhubarb filling under a golden buttery oat crumble.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly butter a baking dish large enough to hold the fruit in an even layer.
Toss rhubarb, strawberries, sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice until the fruit is evenly coated.
Transfer the filling to the dish and level it so it bakes at the same rate throughout.
Rub oats, flour, brown sugar, cinnamon and cold butter together until a chunky crumble forms.
Scatter the topping loosely over the fruit and bake until golden with bubbling juices at the edges.
Rest the crisp for at least 15 minutes so the filling thickens, then serve warm with ice cream.
tips: Use firm rhubarb stalks for a bright filling.
substitutions: Use frozen strawberries after draining excess liquid.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to three days.
